First release of Sub-Crate, a standalone Rust backend compatible with Sub-Store.

## New Features

- Run the backend without Node.js. Rust handles HTTP, storage, subscription and rule conversion, built-in processors, scheduling, backup and synchronization.
- Use the official Sub-Store frontend without source changes. Open the [hosted frontend](https://sub-store.vercel.app/subs) or obtain it from the [official frontend project](https://github.com/sub-store-org/Sub-Store-Front-End).
- Run general JavaScript scripts through the embedded QuickJS engine, including the supported storage, network and conversion helpers.
- Download native Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64 backend packages. Docker images for both Linux architectures are available from GHCR.

## Compatibility

- Existing JSON data files and frontend API conventions are retained. Back up your data before migrating, and run only one backend against a writable data directory.
- Node.js built-ins, `require`/npm package loading, `process.env`, `$substore.node` and native addons are excluded. Choose a script's general JavaScript variant when available.
- Native Linux binaries require glibc 2.38 or newer. Use the GHCR image when the host libraries do not meet the native package requirements.

## Downloads

Release attachments contain three native backend archives and `SHA256SUMS`. Each archive includes startup instructions, license notices and a link to its exact source. Build manifests remain in Actions artifacts.

Pull `ghcr.io/dslzl/sub-crate:v0.0.1` (also tagged `0.0.1` and `latest`). The image supports `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. Installation, frontend hosting, configuration and rollback instructions are in the packaged README or [rust/README.md](https://github.com/DSLZL/Sub-Crate/blob/v0.0.1/rust/README.md).
